Cette enquête inédite met en lumière le rôle central de Sipan Hemo dans la recomposition sécuritaire et politique du Nord-Est syrien. Elle analyse les défis auxquels il est confronté, entre intégration des forces kurdes, tensions régionales et rivalités internes, tout en soulignant son profil pragmatique et sa capacité à naviguer dans un environnement complexe. turkish intelligence (@turkish_intell) Sipan Hemo: From the YPG to a Central Figure in Syria’s New Architecture 1/2 The appointment of Sipan Hemo as Deputy Minister of Defense for northeastern Syria, officially confirmed on March 10, immediately places him at the center of major security and political challenges. A former Commander-in-Chief of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), he is now tasked with a particularly sensitive mission: integrating Kurdish forces into the military apparatus of the new Syrian regime, while managing an unstable regional environment marked by tensions between Iran and Israel. From the very first weeks of his tenure, Hemo has been confronted with a series of attacks targeting military positions in the region. On March 29, the Qasrak base, located in the Kurdish governorate of Hasakah, was struck by drones launched from the Iraqi border. A few days earlier, on March 23, the Kharab al-Jir base had also come under rocket fire, though no casualties were reported, notably due to the prior withdrawal of U.S. forces in February. Hemo was quick to respond publicly, accusing Baghdad, via his new account on X, of failing to effectively control its territory. Now responsible for the Kurdish regions from a military standpoint, he must secure an area still exposed to incursions by pro-Iranian Iraqi militias, particularly active in the context of the conflict opposing Tehran and Tel Aviv since late February. Although relatively spared so far, eastern Syria remains vulnerable to these regional dynamics. Beyond the security dimension, however, Sipan Hemo plays a central role in a long-term political process: the integration of Kurdish forces into Syrian state structures. This project, formalized by an agreement concluded on January 29, had been negotiated following the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024. At the time, Hemo was part of the team led by Mazloum Abdi, tasked with representing Kurdish interests vis-à-vis the new authorities in Damascus. This integration dynamic has also been reflected in symbolic appointments, such as that of Nourredin Issa Ahmed, a former SDF commander, who became governor of Hasakah in February, a first for a Kurd in Syria. However, this process unfolds in a personally difficult context for Hemo, marked by the death of his long-time ally Saleh Muslim, who passed away on March 11 in Erbil and was also expected to play a role in the new security architecture. On the ground, tensions remain high. Prior to the ceasefire negotiated under the auspices of U.S. envoy Tom Barrack, clashes between the SDF and forces stemming from Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), led by Ahmed al-Charaa, were nearly constant. In this context, Sipan Hemo’s profile appears to be an asset. Considered moderate and pragmatic, he embodies a conciliatory approach, in contrast to more controversial figures such as Azad Simi, head of SDF intelligence, who is viewed as too polarizing, particularly by Ankara. Turkey, a key supporter of HTS in its takeover of Damascus, remains strongly hostile to the SDF, which it equates with the PKK. Hemo must therefore cooperate with former adversaries, notably Awad al-Jassim, also known as Abu Qutaiba al-Manbiji, commander of the Syrian army’s 60th Brigade, in order to integrate Kurdish fighters into national military structures. His ability to defuse tensions has already been demonstrated, particularly in January, when he called for calm following the rapid loss of the Kurdish neighborhoods of Ashrafieh and Sheikh Maqsoud in Aleppo, thereby preventing a broader escalation. His role, however, extends beyond the strictly military dimension. Authorities in Damascus are also relying on him to mobilize the intelligence networks developed by the SDF over the past decade, particularly within local tribes. These networks are essential for stabilizing a region where the threat of the Islamic State remains latent, especially in camps where former fighters are detained. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/turkish_intell/status/2042186726500708716#m

Es que el invierno puede favorecer la deshidratación debido a factores como la menor sensación de sed, el uso de calefacción y la sequedad ambiental. In our latest @ForeignPolicy piece, @hamid_dahouei and I argue: The Iran war was not just about oil, missiles, or Hormuz. It exposed something far more consequential: the physical vulnerability of the infrastructure powering the AI age. What we call “the cloud” is not abstract. It is fixed, territorial, and targetable. Data centers, worth billions, can be disrupted by drones costing a few thousand dollars. In the recent years, the GCC was imagined as a future global hub for AI infrastructure, backed by capital, energy, and U.S. security guarantees. But this vision rested on a flawed assumption: that capital and alliances could override geography. The war shattered that assumption. Once AI infrastructure became embedded in great-power competition, it ceased to be purely economic, it became strategic, and therefore a target. The deeper lesson is clear: technology does not escape geopolitics. Infrastructure follows geography, and geography ultimately determines what can survive. The future of AI will be decided by one question: who can protect compute, and where. foreignpolicy.com/2026/04/10…

According to unconfirmed reports: • The US has authorized the release of $6 billion dollars in frozen Iranian funds • A ceasefire will be implemented in Lebanon These are apparently the preconditions for Iran to start talks tomorrow.

Decades of diplomacy failed to ease sanctions on Iran, but 40 days of war shifted the balance—$6 billion in frozen assets getting released, sanctions are easing, and Iran is gaining leverage over the Strait of Hormuz, pushing it closer to global power status.

The main asymmetry is that Iran appears to have a better alternative to a negotiated agreement than does the US: In the absence of a deal, strikes on Iran will resume, but with diminishing marginal returns for the US, while the closure of the Strait will persist, with growing marginal returns for Iran. It doesn't mean Iran won't pay a significant price in the event talks collapse, which is a good reason why they agreed to them. It means that, rightly or wrongly, Iran feels it can sustain the price of a breakdown longer and better than the US can. Danny (Dennis) Citrinowicz ,داني سيترينوفيتش (@citrinowicz) Recent moves suggest a clear asymmetry going into U.S.–Iran talks: The U.S. appears to be: 1. Backing away from its own ultimatum 2. Pressuring Pakistan to broker a ceasefire (and helping draft the message) 3. Urging Israel to halt operations in Lebanon 4. Largely overlooking the closure of the Strait of Hormuz 5. Signaling willingness to release frozen Iranian funds 6. Indicating that talks will be based on Iran’s original 10- points framework 7. Sending the vice president for the discussions with a regime it tried to topple Iran, meanwhile, simply shows up to the talks, and even didn't "open" the Straits as agreed. While the administration’s effort to pursue a diplomatic solution and halt the cycle of escalation is commendable, The real issue is that Tehran likely assume it is entering the talks from a position of strength. Ultimately, the administration will have to make a choice: accept a deal on terms largely shaped by Iran framed as a “gracious compromise”, or stand firm on its principles at the risk of another round of escalation. At this stage, the least probable scenario to envision is Iran backing down. Since Iran has taken a significant blow with serious economic consequences that shouldn’t be underestimated, Any agreement will, almost by definition, strengthen the regime. At the same time, another round of conflict is unlikely to bring it down, and its costs will only continue to rise. Still, at this stage, it appears that one side is more eager to reach an agreement. We will soon see whether, and how, that urgency translates into actual progress at the negotiating table. This is an interesting conversation and I want to hop on board it. tl;dr not the same, just as effective for the goal intended, supply chain attacks more common, ooga booga not good Jiri and Georgy are correct (sort of, in my opinion), but I also disagree with some of their assertions. STX Rat has some really cool and interesting features that I don't typically see in malware. I unironically think it being written in several different languages, compiling in-line, and the consistent in-memory execution is really interesting. I like it. It isn't super novel, but it's got enough unique characteristics to show some sort of effort is invested. I am super biased though because I love malware of all shapes and sizes, I appreciate it for what it is. What was absolutely atrocious was how botched the execution of this supply-chain attack was. I was immediately able to identify the actor because they recycled the C2 domain. I have no idea why they did that, but that was terrible from an OPSEC perspective. They can compromise a well known domain but can't afford $9 for a new domain name? Additionally, they butchered the installer. It was the broken installation wizard that caused it to be detected (or rather, raise suspicion) from end users. Once it was given the side eye from end users the whole operation imploded and ended in less than 6 hours. Ultimately, comparing this to a long-term state-sponsored espionage campaign is not a fair comparison. They're not the same and do not possess the same end-goal. The recent trend of supply-chain attacks are designed for smash-and-grab. Yes, they're less sophisticated, but they're still effective. I'm not sure what that says about the state of cybersecurity, but a smash-and-grab campaign is more attractive to financially motivated Threat Actors than long-term missions. Jiří Vinopal (@vinopaljiri) Tbh, the last few months of supply-chain attacks have shown a clear drop in novelty and malware quality. ☹️ Most of it barely hits average offensive standards - 💯% disappointment from a reverse-engineering POV. Still, the rising number of these ops and the underlying trends are dead serious. We can’t ignore them. Need to keep checking every single one. Sipan Hemo: From the YPG to a Central Figure in Syria’s New Architecture 1/2 The appointment of Sipan Hemo as Deputy Minister of Defense for northeastern Syria, officially confirmed on March 10, immediately places him at the center of major security and political challenges. A former Commander-in-Chief of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), he is now tasked with a particularly sensitive mission: integrating Kurdish forces into the military apparatus of the new Syrian regime, while managing an unstable regional environment marked by tensions between Iran and Israel. From the very first weeks of his tenure, Hemo has been confronted with a series of attacks targeting military positions in the region. On March 29, the Qasrak base, located in the Kurdish governorate of Hasakah, was struck by drones launched from the Iraqi border. A few days earlier, on March 23, the Kharab al-Jir base had also come under rocket fire, though no casualties were reported, notably due to the prior withdrawal of U.S. forces in February. Hemo was quick to respond publicly, accusing Baghdad, via his new account on X, of failing to effectively control its territory. Now responsible for the Kurdish regions from a military standpoint, he must secure an area still exposed to incursions by pro-Iranian Iraqi militias, particularly active in the context of the conflict opposing Tehran and Tel Aviv since late February. Although relatively spared so far, eastern Syria remains vulnerable to these regional dynamics. Beyond the security dimension, however, Sipan Hemo plays a central role in a long-term political process: the integration of Kurdish forces into Syrian state structures. This project, formalized by an agreement concluded on January 29, had been negotiated following the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024. At the time, Hemo was part of the team led by Mazloum Abdi, tasked with representing Kurdish interests vis-à-vis the new authorities in Damascus. This integration dynamic has also been reflected in symbolic appointments, such as that of Nourredin Issa Ahmed, a former SDF commander, who became governor of Hasakah in February, a first for a Kurd in Syria. However, this process unfolds in a personally difficult context for Hemo, marked by the death of his long-time ally Saleh Muslim, who passed away on March 11 in Erbil and was also expected to play a role in the new security architecture. On the ground, tensions remain high. Prior to the ceasefire negotiated under the auspices of U.S. envoy Tom Barrack, clashes between the SDF and forces stemming from Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), led by Ahmed al-Charaa, were nearly constant. In this context, Sipan Hemo’s profile appears to be an asset. Considered moderate and pragmatic, he embodies a conciliatory approach, in contrast to more controversial figures such as Azad Simi, head of SDF intelligence, who is viewed as too polarizing, particularly by Ankara. Turkey, a key supporter of HTS in its takeover of Damascus, remains strongly hostile to the SDF, which it equates with the PKK. Hemo must therefore cooperate with former adversaries, notably Awad al-Jassim, also known as Abu Qutaiba al-Manbiji, commander of the Syrian army’s 60th Brigade, in order to integrate Kurdish fighters into national military structures. His ability to defuse tensions has already been demonstrated, particularly in January, when he called for calm following the rapid loss of the Kurdish neighborhoods of Ashrafieh and Sheikh Maqsoud in Aleppo, thereby preventing a broader escalation. His role, however, extends beyond the strictly military dimension. Authorities in Damascus are also relying on him to mobilize the intelligence networks developed by the SDF over the past decade, particularly within local tribes. These networks are essential for stabilizing a region where the threat of the Islamic State remains latent, especially in camps where former fighters are detained.

Cette enquête inédite met en lumière le rôle central de Sipan Hemo dans la recomposition sécuritaire et politique du Nord-Est syrien. Elle analyse les défis auxquels il est confronté, entre intégration des forces kurdes, tensions régionales et rivalités internes, tout en soulignant son profil pragmatique et sa capacité à naviguer dans un environnement complexe. turkish intelligence (@turkish_intell) Sipan Hemo: From the YPG to a Central Figure in Syria’s New Architecture 1/2 The appointment of Sipan Hemo as Deputy Minister of Defense for northeastern Syria, officially confirmed on March 10, immediately places him at the center of major security and political challenges. A former Commander-in-Chief of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF), he is now tasked with a particularly sensitive mission: integrating Kurdish forces into the military apparatus of the new Syrian regime, while managing an unstable regional environment marked by tensions between Iran and Israel. From the very first weeks of his tenure, Hemo has been confronted with a series of attacks targeting military positions in the region. On March 29, the Qasrak base, located in the Kurdish governorate of Hasakah, was struck by drones launched from the Iraqi border. A few days earlier, on March 23, the Kharab al-Jir base had also come under rocket fire, though no casualties were reported, notably due to the prior withdrawal of U.S. forces in February. Hemo was quick to respond publicly, accusing Baghdad, via his new account on X, of failing to effectively control its territory. Now responsible for the Kurdish regions from a military standpoint, he must secure an area still exposed to incursions by pro-Iranian Iraqi militias, particularly active in the context of the conflict opposing Tehran and Tel Aviv since late February. Although relatively spared so far, eastern Syria remains vulnerable to these regional dynamics. Beyond the security dimension, however, Sipan Hemo plays a central role in a long-term political process: the integration of Kurdish forces into Syrian state structures. This project, formalized by an agreement concluded on January 29, had been negotiated following the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024. At the time, Hemo was part of the team led by Mazloum Abdi, tasked with representing Kurdish interests vis-à-vis the new authorities in Damascus. This integration dynamic has also been reflected in symbolic appointments, such as that of Nourredin Issa Ahmed, a former SDF commander, who became governor of Hasakah in February, a first for a Kurd in Syria. However, this process unfolds in a personally difficult context for Hemo, marked by the death of his long-time ally Saleh Muslim, who passed away on March 11 in Erbil and was also expected to play a role in the new security architecture. On the ground, tensions remain high. Prior to the ceasefire negotiated under the auspices of U.S. envoy Tom Barrack, clashes between the SDF and forces stemming from Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), led by Ahmed al-Charaa, were nearly constant. In this context, Sipan Hemo’s profile appears to be an asset. Considered moderate and pragmatic, he embodies a conciliatory approach, in contrast to more controversial figures such as Azad Simi, head of SDF intelligence, who is viewed as too polarizing, particularly by Ankara. Turkey, a key supporter of HTS in its takeover of Damascus, remains strongly hostile to the SDF, which it equates with the PKK. Hemo must therefore cooperate with former adversaries, notably Awad al-Jassim, also known as Abu Qutaiba al-Manbiji, commander of the Syrian army’s 60th Brigade, in order to integrate Kurdish fighters into national military structures. His ability to defuse tensions has already been demonstrated, particularly in January, when he called for calm following the rapid loss of the Kurdish neighborhoods of Ashrafieh and Sheikh Maqsoud in Aleppo, thereby preventing a broader escalation. His role, however, extends beyond the strictly military dimension. Authorities in Damascus are also relying on him to mobilize the intelligence networks developed by the SDF over the past decade, particularly within local tribes. These networks are essential for stabilizing a region where the threat of the Islamic State remains latent, especially in camps where former fighters are detained. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/turkish_intell/status/2042186726500708716#m

His Excellency Mohammed bin Abdullah Al-Jadaan, Finance Minister of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, who was on a one-day visit to Islamabad called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif at the Prime Minister House this evening. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Muhammad Ishaq Dar and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir also attended the meeting. Welcoming the Saudi dignitary, the Prime Minister conveyed his respectful regards to The Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, His Majesty King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and His Royal Highness Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud. The Prime Minister fondly recalled his recent warm and cordial telephone conversation with His Royal Highness the Crown Prince. He expressed appreciation for the Crown Prince’s deep affection towards Pakistan as well as for the Kingdom's longstanding economic and financial support to Pakistan over the years, that had played a vital role in Pakistan's economic stability. The Prime Minister reiterated that the people and Government of Pakistan had always stood shoulder to shoulder with their Saudi brothers and sisters at all times, and this was an abiding bond between both countries, that had grown stronger under the patronage of His Royal Highness the Crown Prince. The Prime Minister emphasized Pakistan’s strong commitment to expanding its cooperation with the Kingdom in all spheres, particularly in trade, investment, and economic development. The Saudi Finance Minister thanked the Prime Minister and reaffirmed the resolve of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to further strengthen the longstanding deep-rooted fraternal bonds between Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, as envisioned by His Royal Highness Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. नारी शक्ति वंदन अधिनियम आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री @narendramodi जी स्वयं आकर इसके बारे में बात करते हैं और वीडियो के माध्यम से हम बहनों को संदेश देते हैं। आज भारत को आगे बढ़ाने के लिए महिलाओं का आगे आना आवश्यक है। केवल विकास ही नहीं, बल्कि देश को सही दिशा में ले जाने की भी जरूरत है। आज संसद, असेंबली और विधानसभाओं में महिलाएं आगे आकर सत्ता का हिस्सा बनें, शासन और प्रशासन में भागीदारी निभाएं, यह बहुत जरूरी है। एक महिला और एक बेटी होने के नाते, हमने अपने जीवन में जो देखा और सहा है, वही हमें बेहतर निर्णय लेने की समझ देता है। जब यह निर्णय लिया गया कि बेटियों को साइकिल दी जाए, ताकि वे आसानी से स्कूल जा सकें, तब मुझे वह संघर्ष याद आया जो एक बेटी को जन्म से आगे बढ़ने तक करना पड़ता है। इसी सोच के साथ “लखपति बिटिया योजना” लाई गई, ताकि हर बेटी पढ़े, अपनी ग्रेजुएशन पूरी करे और अपने पैरों पर खड़ी हो सके। जब यह नीति बनाई गई, तो उसे एक महिला के दृष्टिकोण से आगे बढ़ाया गया। मेरा मानना है कि देश की हर जागरूक महिला को आगे आकर इस बिल पर अपनी राय देनी चाहिए, इसका समर्थन करना चाहिए और अपनी भूमिका तय करनी चाहिए। मैं दिल की गहराइयों से केंद्र सरकार और आदरणीय प्रधानमंत्री जी का धन्यवाद करती हूं, जिन्होंने हम बहनों को इतना बड़ा सम्मान और अधिकार देने का कार्य किया। #NariShaktiVandan Video

Instead of relying solely on the front cameras, the system estimates the physical friction between the rubber wiper blade and the glass by analyzing the motor’s electrical power consumption. Additionally, it keeps a long-term friction level average to warn when wiper replacements are necessary due to higher than normal friction. Smart stuff! Did you know C.S. Lewis predicted the modern obsession with “being nice” would destroy the soul? In The Abolition of Man, Lewis argues that when a society stops believing in objective virtue, it doesn’t become tolerant… it becomes manipulable. He calls the result “men without chests.” People with appetites and intellects, but no courage, no honor, no trained moral instincts. They can calculate everything and defend nothing. Lewis saw that once we reject inherited moral law, we don’t become free. We become raw material… easily shaped by propaganda, pleasure, and fear. Modern man prides himself on compassion while quietly surrendering every standard that once gave compassion meaning. Lewis’s insight is brutal: a civilization that educates clever cowards will eventually be ruled by tyrants or technicians. Because when nothing is worth dying for, everything becomes negotiable… including human dignity.

Both leaders emphasized the importance of ensuring that the ceasefire remains in place and creates the necessary conditions for lasting peace and stability in the region. The two leaders agreed to work together to lend fresh impetus to the longstanding friendly ties between Pakistan and the United Kingdom, across all spheres of mutual interest. The Prime Minister reiterated his cordial invitation to Prime Minister Starmer to undertake an official visit to Pakistan.

In my view, propriety demands that he should immediately recuse or disassociate himself from the case. It needs to be noted that Seven Member Bench of the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Malik Qayyum Case (reported in 2001 PLD SC 568) held that bias on part of the judge vitiates judicial proceedings. The court further held that an accused has a right of a fair trial by a judicial minded person, not by someone functioning under an influence or bias as the same paralyses his judicial faculties to conduct fair trial. Bias would vitiate judicial proceedings if such circumstances exist. Bias robs the judge of the confidence that a litigant may have in the judge. भाडेतत्त्वावरील घरांसाठी राज्य सरकारचा मोठा निर्णय मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली झोपडपट्टी पुनर्वसन प्राधिकरण बैठक पार पडली. घाटकोपर येथील लोकशाहीर साहित्यरत्न अण्णाभाऊ साठे आंतरराष्ट्रीय स्मारकासाठी ₹332.62 कोटींच्या तरतुदीस मान्यता देण्यात आली असून, या प्रकल्पामुळे बाधित होणाऱ्या अपात्र झोपडी धारकांनासुद्धा भाडेतत्वावरील घरे योजने अंतर्गत देण्यात यावीत. तसेच स्मारकाचे काम गतीने पूर्ण करण्याचे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी दिले. सन 2025 मध्ये निर्गमित करण्यात आलेल्या, राज्य गृहनिर्माण धोरण 2025 अनुषंगाने शासनामार्फत अंमलात आणलेल्या झोपडपट्टी समूह पुनर्विकास योजनेअंतर्गत समूह क्षेत्रांचा एकात्मिक व शाश्वत विकास करण्याचा निर्णय घेतला आहे. यामध्ये 50 एकर किंवा त्यापेक्षा अधिकच्या भूखंडावरील प्रकल्प हे योजनेमध्ये पुनर्विकसीत करण्याचा निर्णय झाला असून, त्याबाबत प्राधिकरणामार्फत समूह क्षेत्र निश्चित करण्याची प्रक्रिया सुरू आहे, याचा आढावा मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांनी घेतला. या योजनेअंतर्गत अंदाजे 6 ते 7 लाख झोपडीधारकांना पुनर्वसनाचा लाभ होणार आहे. माता रमाबाई आंबेडकर नगर आणि कामराज नगर येथील योजनेसाठी अतिरिक्त ₹97 कोटींच्या वाढीव निधीस मंजुरी देण्यात आली असून, यासाठी आता एकूण ₹597 कोटींचा निधी आता वापरात येणार आहे. या बैठकीदरम्यान मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी झोपडपट्टी पुनर्वसन योजनेअंतर्गतच्या योजनांमधून उपलब्ध होणाऱ्या प्रकल्पग्रस्त पुनर्वसन सदनिकांचा आढावा घेण्याच्या सूचना दिल्या. झोपडपट्टी प्राधिकरणाच्या वतीने बेकायदेशीर अतिक्रमणाबाबत माहिती मिळावी, यासाठी प्रधानमंत्री गतीशक्ति अभियांनाअंतर्गत ‘नेत्रम’ ही संगणकीय प्रणाली तयार करण्यात आली आहे. याद्वारे सॅटेलाईट छायाचित्रांच्या माध्यमातून मुंबईतील अतिक्रमणांवर लक्ष From mobility and logistics to retail and financial services, this evolution presents both significant opportunities and complex governance challenges. Against this backdrop, 𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐚𝐧 𝐂𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐥 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐑𝐞𝐬𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐜𝐡 𝐨𝐧 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐚𝐥 𝐄𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐨𝐦𝐢𝐜 𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 (𝐈𝐂𝐑𝐈𝐄𝐑) in collaboration with The Dialogue, is convening a high-level, in-person conference to initiate a 𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐝, 𝐦𝐮𝐥𝐭𝐢-𝐬𝐭𝐚𝐤𝐞𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐚𝐥𝐨𝐠𝐮𝐞 on navigating India’s platform economy. The conference will also mark the launch of the 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦 𝐄𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐨𝐦𝐲 𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐮𝐦, a collaborative initiative that brings together 𝐠𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭, 𝐢𝐧𝐝𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐲, 𝐚𝐜𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐦𝐢𝐚, and 𝐜𝐢𝐯𝐢𝐥 𝐬𝐨𝐜𝐢𝐞𝐭𝐲 to support the 𝘳𝘦𝘴𝘱𝘰𝘯𝘴𝘪𝘣𝘭𝘦, 𝘴𝘶𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘪𝘯𝘢𝘣𝘭𝘦, and 𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘭𝘶𝘴𝘪𝘷𝘦 evolution of platform ecosystems.
